summary: At five in the morning on the nineteenth of Harvestside, following the resolution of the pond dispute, the grove encounter with Shambly, and approximately four to five hours of what Waluigi describes as 'cumulative operational activity' and what everyone else describes as 'chaos,' the party entered Ferngrove Manor's L-shaped lounge and found Wario at the bar. Wario revealed he had taken coins from a well and aged papers from a woman's room, showed them an extradimensional leather bag stuffed with everything he had accumulated, and offered to sell the information for five gold. Hjumpik demanded the papers back. Wario asked for twenty gold. Hjumpik pointed out that Wario had stolen them. Wario offered Fey brandy. Hjumpik tackled him and retrieved the papers, which turned out to include what Wario claimed was Princess Peach's original cake recipe — authenticity deeply questionable, genuinely functional, flagged for analysis — and Toad Lee only then realized he had possessed the aged papers the entire time. Wario offered Toad Lee two hundred gold for them, then knocked twice on Hjumpik's back with a confusing thumbs up, then offered to release Waluigi's considerable debt in exchange for the papers, identifying the potential buyer as a large crowned Toad who had offered him a fragment of the Chaos Heart. This revelation was not satisfyingly explained. Waluigi proposed making a copy and handing the original over. Hjumpik refused. Nobody paid the debt. Wario did not care. Then, in the sequence of events that defines this entry: Toad Lee and Hjumpik fought over the papers, a badminton shuttlecock flew across the room, Waluigi intercepted it with fire in his eyes, ran away with it, slammed directly into Hjumpik and was damaged by his own flaming shuttlecock, apologized, ran again toward Wario's helicopter, admitted he had taken it a bit far but the prospect of not donating both kidneys was appealing, and eventually a handoff was arranged through Rakasha as third party, Wario ate a stack of papers that only Waluigi noticed, the real papers were handed to Rakasha and then returned to Saedia, and Waluigi cried on the floor while Wario walked away referencing clients to see. The entry is written by Waluigi. Waluigi is aware of the conflict of interest. Waluigi is doing his best. WAH.
description:
Waluigi must begin this entry with a declaration that he is aware this entry has a conflict of interest problem and that the conflict of interest problem is him.

Waluigi was directly involved in the events documented here. Waluigi had personal financial stakes in the outcome. Waluigi performed the action that is, by consensus of everyone present, the least defensible thing he has done during the entire Feyward campaign. Waluigi then ran into Hjumpik while carrying a flaming shuttlecock and was injured by it, which is either cosmic justice or poor spatial awareness or both.

Waluigi is still going to write this entry, because if Waluigi does not write it, nobody will, and if nobody writes it, history will record only that 'some papers changed hands at five in the morning' and leave out the kidneys entirely. The kidneys are important. The kidneys explain everything. Or they explain Waluigi's decision, which is not the same as justifying it, but is at least the kind of context that makes a person say 'oh' instead of 'why.'

The reader should approach this entry with the understanding that Waluigi is attempting objectivity while being constitutionally unsuited to objectivity in his own defense and existentially incapable of making himself look worse than he already does. Waluigi has tried to include the parts where he was wrong. They are there. They are not flattering. Waluigi is including them because history deserves them even when Waluigi does not deserve to be in history quite this specifically.

WAH.

## Preliminary Note on Waluigi's Debt


Before documenting the events of the lounge, Waluigi must explain the debt, because the debt is the engine that drove everything that followed and it does not make sense without context.

Waluigi has debts. Waluigi has many debts. Some of them are legitimate and Waluigi is working on them. Some of them are what Wario calls 'partnership expenses' accrued during a period of joint business ventures that Waluigi considers deeply mischaracterized in the ledger. Some of them are the product of compound interest applied to the original amounts at rates that Waluigi believes would make a usurer uncomfortable. Some of them are line items labeled 'Wario Brand Services Rendered' that Waluigi has never been able to get Wario to itemize despite repeated requests.

The total amount is, in Waluigi's current financial position, catastrophic.

The method by which Waluigi has been informed he must pay a portion of this debt involves his kidneys. Specifically: half the debt can apparently be settled in kind through what Waluigi's creditors have described as 'organic asset liquidation,' which is a phrase that sounds administrative until you understand that it means one of Waluigi's kidneys.

Waluigi has two kidneys. He would like to keep both of them. This is, Waluigi believes, a reasonable preference. He is not asking for special treatment. He is asking for the same standard of organ retention that most people in the Doughnut World take for granted and that Waluigi is apparently one document negotiation away from losing.

This is the context. When the papers arrived and Wario offered Waluigi's debt as a bargaining chip, Waluigi did not react with measured professional detachment. Waluigi reacted like a man who has been carrying the knowledge that his kidneys are in play for longer than anyone in this party knew, who suddenly saw a door and ran for it without stopping to check what was on the other side.

This does not make what Waluigi did right. It makes it comprehensible. Waluigi is doing his best with comprehensible.

## The Lounge: Setting and Wario


The L-shaped lounge of Ferngrove Manor was, by the standards of the feyward manor and the preceding several hours of operations, genuinely comfortable. Worn but well-cared-for furnishings. Bookshelves along most of the walls. A long carpet running the main length of the room over which four small loungers with side tables were arranged to watch a small stage with a piano and a standing harp. In the corner, a messy bar stocked with an impressive selection of drinks, two giant kegs, and enough seating for eight. A goblin staffer manned the bar with the professional composure of someone who had seen everything and decided not to be surprised anymore.

Everything was free of charge.

Waluigi, upon entering a room where everything was free of charge at five in the morning after fighting a plant monster and witnessing a confession of sustained cosmetic crime, found the atmosphere deeply suspicious. Free drinks in a fey manor at five AM are either hospitality or a trap. Waluigi has learned the hard way that the Feywild does not distinguish meaningfully between those two categories.

Wario was at the bar.

Wario was there in the full sense of the word there — not visiting the bar, not passing through, not having a quick drink before leaving, but OCCUPYING the bar with the settled territorial confidence of a man who had identified the best position in the room, claimed it, and was now conducting business from it. He had arranged himself at the seat that commanded the best sightline to both entrances, had a drink in one hand, and was in the middle of commenting on how thoroughly Hjumpik's party had cleared out whatever room they had been investigating.

'You really cleared out that room over there,' Wario said. 'I took the coins in the well.'

Hjumpik asked if there had been anything else of value.

Wario said five gold and he would tell them.

Hjumpik pointed out that they had defeated the monster.

Wario, honoring the spirit of commercial negotiation, accepted this argument by producing the information for free. He had retrieved an aged parchment from the woman's room and three figures of gold. He then showed them a large leather sack.

Waluigi recognized the bag immediately. It was an extradimensional storage device — the kind that looks too light for its apparent size and opens into impossible depths. The original owner's initials had been scratched out aggressively. The bag was, by Waluigi's estimation, absolutely stuffed with everything. Coins. Weapons. Food. Magical items. Junk. More coins. Something that smelled like old cheese. Possibly a cursed artifact or two, because Wario does not carefully screen acquisitions for negative enchantments as long as they have sufficient resale value.

Waluigi has seen this bag before. Waluigi has reason to believe the scratched-out initials begin with a W and are not Wario's W. Waluigi is not going to press this here because some battles are not worth the energy at five in the morning.

## The Peach Cake Recipe: Authentication Notes and Wario's Business Model


Hjumpik demanded the parchment paper.

Wario asked for twenty gold.

Hjumpik said no, Wario had stolen it.

Wario offered Fey brandy.

Hjumpik tackled him. Waluigi wants to document this as a real thing that happened: a dwarf tackled Wario in a feyward lounge at five in the morning over a piece of paper. Hjumpik weighs considerably less than Wario. The tackle succeeded anyway, because Hjumpik commits to physical engagement with the same completeness he commits to everything else, and because Wario, despite his considerable mass and combat capability, was apparently not expecting to be tackled by his own bar stool. Hjumpik snatched the paper and stood back up.

The paper, once examined, turned out to be Wario's claim to an aged parchment covered in recipe instructions, measurements, and what appeared to be flour handprints. Wario's claim: this was the original, authentic recipe for Princess Peach's legendary cake. The cake famous throughout the pre-war Mushroom Kingdom. Served at royal functions. Considered one of the great culinary achievements of the era before everything became a civil war.

Waluigi's assessment of the authenticity claim, delivered here with full awareness that Wario has made similar claims before:

The handwriting is too elegant to be Wario's, which counts for something. The royal seal watermark is visible when held to light and matches Peach-era documentation formats that Waluigi has cross-referenced in his investigation files. The marginal notes — 'His Majesty preferred extra strawberries,' 'Princess requests heart-shaped decoration for festivals' — contain the specific mundane domestic detail that forgers rarely bother with because mundane domestic detail feels insufficiently dramatic for a fake royal document.

However: the parchment's age is inconsistent. It looks old, but not eighty-five-plus years old. Several ingredients listed did not become available in the Mushroom Kingdom until after Peach's death. And Wario acquired it during a looting expedition to Peach's Castle ruins in approximately 1005 BF, which he describes as 'found it in the royal kitchens in a waterproof container,' which is exactly what someone who fabricated a recipe says when asked where they found it.

Wario has also created multiple certified copies that he sells for five hundred gold each, claiming they are authorized reproductions.

They are transcriptions he made himself.

The recipe does, apparently, produce a genuinely good cake regardless of its origin. Waluigi has not tested this personally. Waluigi is documenting Wario's position on the matter: 'Does it matter WHERE the recipe came from if the cake tastes amazing? No! Stop asking questions and pay me!'

This is not a historical methodology that Waluigi endorses. It is, Waluigi admits, not entirely wrong as a pragmatic position on culinary provenance.

## The Aged Papers: Toad Lee's


Inventory Failure and Wario's Opening Bid

While Hjumpik was examining the cake recipe and Wario was calculating whether the tackle had improved or damaged his negotiating position, Toad Lee had a realization.

The aged papers — the documents Saedia needed for the unaging ritual, the papers that had been the operational objective of the Ferngrove mission — were in his possession. Had been in his possession. Toad Lee had apparently been carrying them the entire time without fully registering their presence in his inventory.

Waluigi finds this simultaneously understandable and deeply irritating. Understandable because the preceding several hours involved a pond argument, a grove monster, a confession of decades-long cosmetic crime, a dragon revelation, a Rakasha disappearing through a portal, and approximately four to five hours of cumulative feyward disorientation. In those circumstances, misremembering what you have in your pockets is forgivable. Irritating because the papers were the MISSION OBJECTIVE and their location should have been confirmed at multiple points during the mission.

Wario saw Toad Lee's realization and made his first commercial move: two hundred gold for the papers.

Toad Lee did not immediately respond.

Wario, recognizing that direct negotiation was producing slow results, tried a different approach. He walked around to Hjumpik's back and knocked on it twice. He gave a confusing thumbs up. Whether this was intended as a signal, a greeting, a physical assessment of Hjumpik's structural integrity, or something else entirely is not clear from any account Waluigi has accessed. Hjumpik's response to being knocked on is not recorded. Waluigi suspects Hjumpik treated it as the behavior of someone who had been in a feyward manor too long and did not ask follow-up questions.

Wario then played his actual card.

'So how about this — I'll release Waluigi of his debts for those papers.'

## The Chaos Heart and the Crowned Toad

The party's immediate reaction was reasonable skepticism. Releasing Waluigi's debts is not a small offer. Waluigi's debts are, as established, catastrophic. The debt involves kidneys. The offer of full debt release in exchange for aged papers suggested either that Wario valued the papers enormously, that the papers had a buyer willing to pay enough to make the debt forgiveness worthwhile, or that Wario was lying.

Hjumpik asked who the potential buyer was.

Wario said it was a big Toad. Like the one behind them. But wearing a crown.

Hjumpik asked if it was Ornelaus Corvinarus.

Wario said no. This one wore a crown. He had offered something Wario couldn't refuse.

Hjumpik asked what had been offered.

Wario, in the manner of someone who has decided that the information might help him get what he wants faster, disclosed it: a fragment of the Chaos Heart.

The room processed this for a moment.

Hjumpik asked what the Chaos Heart was.

Waluigi, who has been documenting this crisis for longer than most people have been aware the crisis exists, can confirm that the Chaos Heart is an artifact of considerable and extremely dangerous significance connected to events in the Doughnut World's deeper history. It is the kind of object that a crowned Toad of sufficient power might possess fragments of and might use as payment for intelligence gathering. It is also the kind of object whose presence as a negotiating incentive implies that the buyer understands the Chaos Heart's function well enough to weaponize access to it as currency.

This is an enormous intelligence data point that the party did not adequately follow up on because the conversation immediately pivoted to the more pressing local problem of Waluigi's kidneys.

Waluigi understands why they pivoted. Waluigi is the one with the kidneys. Waluigi still thinks they should have pushed harder on the crowned Toad.

Hjumpik's summary of the offer was blunt: using Waluigi's debt to reduce pressure on someone else was a new low. Wario's response was to acknowledge this cheerfully — 'Oh what can I say, bad guys like getting paid' — and produce a laugh that managed to be both completely sincere and deeply disarming.

Waluigi notes that 'Wahahaha' is the linguistic equivalent of a fire door. It closes the conversation while technically remaining open.

Waluigi then proposed what he considered a reasonable compromise: make a copy of the papers and give Wario the copy. This would satisfy the buyer's presumed need for the information while preserving Saedia's original documents and resolving the debt.

Hjumpik said no.

Waluigi accepted this.

Waluigi accepted this in the way that a person accepts a ruling they disagree with when they do not yet have enough authority or leverage to contest it — which is to say, outwardly and temporarily. The internal acceptance did not stick. Waluigi was still thinking about the kidneys. Waluigi would be thinking about the kidneys for the remainder of the incident.

## The Arrival of Stucky: An


Interlude in Observed Character

Before the brawl, Waluigi must document what occurred between Hjumpik and Steely, because it is one of the more unexpectedly human moments in the Feyward campaign and it deserves more than a footnote.

Steely — the mechanical dog, Remi's dog, the device that had been traveling with the party in a context that nobody had fully sorted out yet in terms of custody and care — was petted by Hjumpik. This is a simple statement that contains more warmth than Waluigi expected to find at five in the morning in a feyward lounge.

Hjumpik and Steely have developed something. The mechanical animal responds to him. Hjumpik responds back. In a campaign full of supernatural entities, ancient bloodline conspiracies, and extradimensional crises, a dwarf and a mechanical dog finding a moment of uncomplicated warmth is the kind of detail Waluigi documents because it is true and because the true things are often the quietest.

Then something happened. The party apparently received an image — a visual document, a photograph or magical capture of some kind — from when Steely or someone connected to Steely was first transformed or activated or encountered. Waluigi does not have full clarity on what the image showed or how it was received. What he does have is Hjumpik's reported reaction upon seeing it: horrified.

Waluigi does not know what horrified Hjumpik. Waluigi is filing this under 'unresolved significant data requiring follow-up' alongside the crowned Toad and the Chaos Heart fragment, because things that horrify Hjumpik tend to be things that horrify everyone eventually. Hjumpik's horror threshold is high. When it is exceeded, the cause is usually worth knowing.

Then Stucky arrived.

Stucky — who also goes by Stuckina, though she expressed a preference for 'Stucky' in this context, then added 'although I could stick to you' while winking at Hjumpik — arrived in the lounge and immediately produced the specific atmospheric disruption that supernatural beings with unconventional appearances and excellent comic timing tend to produce. Her horrific appearance, as Waluigi's sources describe it, left the Toads present briefly speechless.

Hjumpik, noting that the mermaid who had been watching them earlier was no longer doing so — specifically, the mermaid who had stolen the beauty, Herniva — informed the group that they appeared to have made it back to the manor without incident.

Hjumpik added: 'Stucky.'

Stucky said she preferred Stucky, yes, though she could stick to someone if necessary, and winked again.

Hjumpik clarified, politely but firmly, that he would prefer they keep this professional, that he was just trying to get this done.

Toad Lee, Waluigi's sources note, appeared to think of something interesting at this point, which will not be further documented here. Waluigi agrees with this editorial decision and finds himself oddly relieved to agree with it.

They walked inside. The lounge received them. Wario was at the bar. The events previously described then occurred in the order previously described.

Waluigi is documenting Stucky's arrival here rather than earlier in the entry because her presence in the lounge during the subsequent brawl is directly relevant: she lost an eye. Temporarily. This matters and will be addressed in the appropriate section.

## The Brawl: Sequence of Events


Waluigi must document the brawl in full because he has a conflict of interest and documenting it fully is the only way to demonstrate that the conflict of interest is not preventing him from honesty.

The brawl began when Toad Lee and Hjumpik began physically contesting the papers. The specific trigger was not a decision or a speech or a dramatic reveal — it was the papers changing hands in an unsafe way and both parties having strong feelings about which direction the papers should travel. Hjumpik was trying to retain them for Saedia. Toad Lee's position in the moment is less clear, though Waluigi suspects he was trying to prevent Hjumpik from doing something impulsive rather than trying to keep the papers for himself.

Wario fell on the floor during the initial physical exchange. This is presented without additional commentary because the image of Wario falling on the floor while a dwarf and a Toad wrestle over historical documents is sufficient on its own terms.

Then the shuttlecock flew.

Waluigi needs to explain the shuttlecock because 'a shuttlecock flew' is not a self-explanatory sentence in most contexts. The lounge had a small stage. The stage had a piano and a standing harp. It was not a sporting arena. Shuttlecocks are not standard lounge equipment. Waluigi does not know where the shuttlecock originated. Waluigi suspects it was a feyward object — the kind of spontaneous sporting equipment that appears in fey spaces when the emotional temperature of the room rises sufficiently and the magic in the walls decides that what the situation needs is a projectile.

The shuttlecock flew across the lounge. Waluigi intercepted it. Waluigi has documented his own action as 'fire in his eyes' because that is how Hjumpik later described the expression on his face, and Hjumpik's descriptions of Waluigi's expressions tend to be more accurate than Waluigi's own self-assessment.

Waluigi ran away with the shuttlecock.

This is the action. This is the betrayal. Not elaborate. Not subtle. Not the product of long planning or careful calculation. Waluigi saw a paper situation that was moving away from resolution, saw an opportunity created by the physical chaos of a lounge brawl, grabbed a burning shuttlecock that he apparently decided was relevant to the papers in some way, and ran.

Waluigi ran directly into Hjumpik.

The shuttlecock was still on fire.

Bowser, in the Corvinarus Sanctum, breathed fire on his own restraints. Waluigi, in a feyward lounge, ran into his teammate while holding a flaming object and was damaged by both the collision and the fire.

Waluigi notes the pattern with the recognition of someone seeing his own reflection for the first time and wishing he had not looked.

Hjumpik said: 'Waluigi — after all we've been through.'

Waluigi said: 'I'm sorry. I'll come back. I promise.'

Toad Lee, skeptically, pointed out that there was no promise and that Waluigi was just going to be trusted.

Wario, seizing the moment with the instinct of someone who has spent decades identifying when other people's chaos creates his openings, called for Waluigi to get to the Wario helicopter and escape. Wario had a helicopter. This is not surprising. Wario has had helicopters before. Waluigi did not ask where the helicopter came from. Waluigi, at this point, was running.

Toad Lee asked if Hjumpik was alright. Hjumpik said yes, he had taken a racket to the face, but he was fine. He wanted the paper back.

Toad Lee could not determine, in the immediate aftermath of the brawl, whether Wario or Waluigi had the real paper. This is a significant detail that will matter shortly.

## Toad Lee's Pursuit and the Cheater's Gambit


Toad Lee ran after Waluigi.

Waluigi, running, was caught. Toad Lee swung his axe — not a full killing blow, but a tactical leg strike designed to stop movement rather than cause maximum harm, which Waluigi notes with the specific gratitude of someone who has been struck by axes and has calibrated opinions about the difference between stopping strikes and other kinds.

The axe hit Waluigi's legs. Another low swing followed. The Cheater's Gambit was deployed.

The Cheater's Gambit is one of Waluigi's signature techniques, a misdirection-based defensive maneuver that exploits opponents' expectations in the same way that Luigi's thunder fake-out exploited Bowser's certainty that the visible buildup was the real attack. Waluigi uses this technique in competition, in confrontation, and apparently in intra-party chases through feyward lounges at five in the morning. The specifics of the gambit's execution in this case are not fully documented, but the general principle is: make them think you are going one direction, go another.

Stucky, observing the chase, took a more direct approach. She removed her eye — the milk-white orb, the one that might be helped by mushrooms and bramble juice and other ingredients Waluigi had mentioned — and threw it at Waluigi.

She missed.

The eye landed on Toad Lee's head.

Waluigi would like to acknowledge that this is an extraordinary sequence of events and that he is aware of his own role in creating the conditions that led to it. A hag removing her eye and throwing it at someone in a lounge because that someone stole papers to avoid paying a kidney debt is the kind of incident that only happens when multiple things have already gone very wrong. Waluigi is responsible for some of those things.

Wario then ground-pounded.

The ground pound — Wario's signature technique, the leap into the air and catastrophic downward impact in sitting position that sends shockwaves radiating outward and cracks the floor and throws everyone nearby off their feet — was deployed in the middle of a feyward manor lounge at five in the morning with, by all accounts, complete enthusiasm. 'WAH HA HA,' Wario bellowed. Clearly pleased with the destruction.

Stucky and Hjumpik almost fell. Stucky grabbed Rakasha's hand. Hjumpik grabbed the nearest stable surface. Azure — Rakasha Azure — caught Wario in an iron grip and held him there while he yelled for help.

Hjumpik, watching all of this, said: 'I'll be back for you.' He looked at Waluigi. 'Time to use my anchor skills.'

Waluigi does not know exactly what Hjumpik's anchor skills involve in this context. Waluigi is fairly certain they involved stopping his own forward momentum to create a stable point for everyone else. This is what Hjumpik does. When everything is moving and nothing is fixed, Hjumpik becomes the fixed thing. He has been doing this the entire campaign.

## The Resolution: Rakasha as Third Party


Somewhere in the chaos of ground pounds, thrown eyes, axe strikes, and helicopter implications, the violence reached its natural endpoint and the conversation resumed.

Toad Lee, approaching Waluigi in the aftermath: 'Come on, Waluigi. It can be another way. It's just money. I don't know you two — there can be another way. Stealing is wrong.'

Waluigi said: 'I think you're right. Why don't we work together as a team?'

Hjumpik said: 'I don't trust you. Give the paper back.'

Waluigi offered a compromise: he would give the paper to a third party.

Hjumpik offered Rakasha Azure as the third party.

Wario asked if anyone liked his Wario bash. Hjumpik said it was alright — Wario had hit him with it. This is one of the more restrained assessments of being hit by a ground pound Waluigi has ever heard.

A handoff was arranged: Rakasha received the paper from Waluigi. Wario produced a stack of papers from somewhere — the extradimensional bag, presumably — and opened his mouth impossibly wide.

He ate them.

Not the actual papers. A stack. The specific stack. Wario ate a stack of papers with the enthusiasm of someone who has never met a food safety regulation and considers chewing sounds an appropriate form of commentary.

Only Waluigi noticed.

Waluigi noticed because Waluigi was watching Wario specifically. Waluigi noticed because Waluigi has been around Wario long enough to know that Wario eating something in the middle of a negotiation is not accidental consumption. It is a move. Wario ate something and looked at Waluigi for a moment and something passed between them that nobody else in the room saw.

Waluigi is not going to fully explain what that look contained in this entry. Some things belong to the operational record rather than the public archive, at least until Waluigi understands them better himself.

Hjumpik applied a mushroom to himself and felt better after the racket to the face. Rakasha confirmed she was a third party when asked by Hjumpik. Papers were examined. Some papers turned to dust — a detail Rakasha reported with the specific calm of someone who has seen magic items deteriorate on contact with the wrong environment and has stopped being surprised by it.

'Why are you a liar, Waluigi?' Toad Lee asked.

Waluigi said: 'That's just my way of doing things.'

Then, after a pause: 'Sorry. But I am a cheater.'

Waluigi means this in the technical sense — the Cheater's Gambit, the misdirection technique, the approach to competition and confrontation that uses expectation against itself. He also means it in the broader sense. Waluigi has spent his life in situations where playing by the rules meant losing, and he has responded to this by becoming someone who identifies which rules can be bent and when. This is not something Waluigi is proud of uniformly. It is something he has accepted about himself with the resignation of a man who has been choosing between his dignity and his kidneys for long enough that the choice has stopped feeling novel.

For a moment, Waluigi's eyes glinted. He showed Hjumpik a stack of papers.

Hjumpik said: 'Yeah, I'm going to need the real stack, please.'

Wario, increasingly annoyed by the declining return on investment, swiped a paper from Waluigi's hands, stared at it for a moment that stretched into what witnesses describe as longer than was comfortable, and then gave it back. 'I got clients to see, money to be made.'

Wario walked away.

Waluigi cried on the floor.

Waluigi is including this because it happened and because the historical record should contain the image of Waluigi on the floor of a feyward lounge at five in the morning having just betrayed his party over a debt he was unable to resolve, being walked away from by Wario, who had already moved on to the next commercial opportunity.

Hjumpik handed the papers back to Saedia.

Saedia, in the way of seneschals who have managed one more impossible night in an impossible manor, pointed to a woman — Stucky, reinserting her eye — and mentioned that there might be a cure involving mushrooms, bramble juice, and a few other ingredients that could be procured.

Then Saedia asked whether they had resolved the dispute she had asked them to resolve.

Hjumpik said he wouldn't say they had, but he had stopped the argument.

Saedia said that was close enough. Then she said she could not sleep with them arguing outside all day, and if it started back up again she did not know what she would do.

Waluigi noted, privately, that it seemed like the hag wanted to kill the mermaid and that there must be a way for them to make up properly. He said this to the group. The group received this suggestion with the energy of people who have been awake for too long and have just watched someone cry on the floor and would like to do one task at a time.

They agreed to talk to the beautiful one — Herniva — and figure it out.

Okay, they said.

## Waluigi's


Assessment: The Conflict of Interest Acknowledged Fully

Waluigi has been asked, implicitly by the act of writing this entry, to assess events in which he was a participant, a stake-holder, a combatant, and the person crying on the floor at the end. Waluigi wants to address the conflict of interest directly rather than pretending it does not exist, because pretending conflicts of interest do not exist is what the Regency does and Waluigi has strong feelings about the Regency.

Could Waluigi be unbiased about these events?

No. Waluigi cannot be fully unbiased about events in which his kidneys were at stake. This is not false modesty. It is the honest acknowledgment that objectivity has limits and personal organ retention is one of them.

Waluigi has tried anyway, because trying matters even when succeeding is impossible, and because the historical record deserves the attempt even if it also deserves a footnote that says the attempt came from someone with strong personal reasons to shade certain facts.

What Waluigi can offer, with confidence, is this:

The debt is real. The kidneys are real. The desperation that produced the shuttlecock theft was real. None of these things make what Waluigi did right. They make it understandable, which is different, and Waluigi is not going to pretend they are the same thing just because the difference is uncomfortable.

Toad Lee was correct that stealing is wrong. Hjumpik was correct not to trust Waluigi immediately after the theft. The fact that Waluigi ultimately allowed the papers to return to Saedia does not retroactively make the attempt noble. It makes it a failure that ended better than it could have.

Wario is also not blameless here, and Waluigi documents this not to deflect responsibility but because it is true. Wario introduced the debt as a negotiating instrument. Wario identified Waluigi's vulnerability and used it. Wario's 'oh what can I say, bad guys like getting paid' is funny in the moment and accurate in its self-description and also a genuine description of the dynamics that put Waluigi on the floor.

The Wario Bros are back in business, some witnesses have said. Waluigi and Wario up to their nefarious deeds again.

Waluigi disputes the characterization. The Wario Bros were never formally disbanded. They were just geographically separated by a dimensional fracture. Whether that constitutes a reunion or a continuation is a matter of classification that Waluigi is not prepared to settle while still in the Feywild.

What Waluigi will say is this: at the end, Waluigi was on the floor and Wario was walking away to see clients, and the difference between those two positions tells you something important about what the Wario Bros arrangement has always been and who has always been paying the higher emotional price to maintain it.

The papers are with Saedia. The debt is unresolved. The kidneys are, for now, still Waluigi's.

The crowned Toad with the Chaos Heart fragment remains unidentified.

Wario ate something that only Waluigi noticed.

These are the facts that matter for the next phase of the investigation.

Everything else — the shuttlecock, the eye, the ground pound, the floor — is context.

Important context.

But context.

WAH.

Waluigi wants that number on the record: FIFTEEN MINUTES from 'let's fix reality' to 'reality is in three pieces and Waluigi is in a fairy dimension surrounded by sentient mushrooms asking him riddles.' The Planar Fracture was not Waluigi's fault. It was the Oracle's ritual, Archie's unstable magic, and everyone's collective decision to IGNORE Waluigi when he raised concerns. Waluigi SAID something. Waluigi raised his hand—his beautiful, well-manicured hand—and said 'Is anyone else concerned about this?' And people SHUSHED him. They SHUSHED Waluigi. The great Waluigi, who was RIGHT, was SHUSHED. description:
Waluigi is going to document this catastrophe in DETAIL because future generations need to understand what happens when you build a reality-altering ritual on a foundation of Archie Miser's magic and optimism.

## The Setup (Where Everything Was Already Wrong)


Raventree Manor was already a problem BEFORE anyone decided to fix it with magic. The building existed across multiple dimensional layers simultaneously—Material Plane, Shadowfell, Feywild, and something called the Deep Mirror that Waluigi still doesn't fully understand and doesn't WANT to understand. The manor's architecture was WRONG. Rooms that shouldn't connect did. Mirrors reflected things that weren't there. Shadows moved independently of their sources.

Waluigi had been saying the manor was dangerous since the FIRST time he saw it. Waluigi noticed the mirrors were wrong. Waluigi noticed the shadows fell at angles that didn't match light sources. Waluigi noticed that the building felt like it was WATCHING. Did anyone listen to Waluigi? Does anyone EVER listen to Waluigi? The answer is no. The answer has ALWAYS been no.

The Oracle—one of multiple Oracles, because apparently ONE mysterious guide wasn't confusing enough—proposed a synchronization ritual. The theory was sound, Waluigi supposes, if you squint at it and ignore all the red flags. Align the three overlapping dimensional layers. Smooth out the planar wrinkles. Stop the wraiths and mirror monsters and general architectural hostility. On PAPER, it probably looked reasonable.

The problem was the EXECUTION.

## The Ritual (Where Waluigi Was Ignored)


The synchronization rite required three things it didn't have:

1. **Coordinated participants** — The party was ARGUING before the ritual started. Multiple people had different ideas about positioning. Nobody agreed on timing.

2. **All required personnel present** — Several key positions in the geometric array were left EMPTY because people were missing, distracted, or refusing to participate.

3. **A stable magical foundation** — And here's where Waluigi needs to pause and SCREAM into the void.

The ritual used ARCHIE MISER'S magic as its primary power source.

ARCHIE. MISER.

The man who resolves diplomatic disputes with FIREBALLS. The man whose magical signature is about as stable as a house of cards in a hurricane during an earthquake on a boat. The man who cast a fireball inside a WOODEN AIRSHIP and acted surprised when people got upset. THAT was the foundation they built the reality-altering ritual on.

Waluigi SAID something. Waluigi specifically raised his hand and asked 'Is anyone else concerned about this?' And people SHUSHED him. They made the 'quiet down' gesture. They told Waluigi to stop being negative. They said everything would be fine.

Fifteen minutes later, reality shattered.

Waluigi would like an apology. Waluigi will not receive one. Waluigi is used to this.

## The Fracture (01:30-01:45, Because Waluigi Checked His Watch)


The ritual began at approximately 01:30 in the morning because apparently nobody considered that maybe reality-altering magic should be performed during BUSINESS HOURS when people are ALERT and have had COFFEE.

For the first few minutes, it seemed to work. The dimensional boundaries around the manor shimmered, flexed, and began to align. Waluigi could feel the planes settling into harmony. It felt like the world exhaling after holding its breath. There was a moment—brief, fragile, almost beautiful—where everything clicked into place.

Then Archie's contribution destabilized.

Because OF COURSE it did.

Waluigi doesn't know the technical magical explanation. What Waluigi KNOWS is that the feedback was instant and catastrophic. The alignment didn't slip gently out of sync—it SHATTERED. Like glass. Like ice on a pond when you step wrong. The dimensional boundaries that were supposed to harmonize instead broke apart, and Raventree Manor—already a nexus of overlapping realities—split into three separate planar fragments.

The room spun. Colors inverted. Sound became light and light became pressure and PRESSURE became a force that picked Waluigi up and threw him sideways through a crack in reality that shouldn't have existed.

Fifteen minutes. From 'this might work' to 'Waluigi is in the Feywild now.' WAH.

## Where Everyone Ended Up (The Cosmic Scatter)


**THE SHADOWFELL — Shadow Estate**

Archie and Bowser were cast into the Shadowfell shard. Waluigi learned about their experience afterward and found it fitting that Archie ended up in the ONE dimension where fire magic doesn't work properly. The Shadowfell's planar physics suppressed fire. Archie without fire is like Waluigi without his hat—technically functional but missing the thing that defines him.

The Shadow Estate was a monochrome version of Raventree Manor. Same architecture, same layout, but drained of color and warmth. Everything in shades of grey and black. The air pressed down like the dimension itself was trying to flatten you into a shadow.

The estate was controlled by the Onyx Hand and their vampire lords—the Corvinarus family's undead branch. Centuries of political intrigue compressed into one haunted manor. The vampires viewed living visitors as either intrusions to punish or diversions to enjoy, and their idea of 'enjoyment' involved forced dinner parties where guests voted on who would die.

**THE FEYWILD — Overgrown Manor**

Waluigi ended up HERE. With Toad Lee. In the FEYWILD.

The Feywild version of Raventree Manor had been consumed by nature in the way nature consumes things when given unlimited time and zero supervision. Walls cracked open by root systems. Corridors choked with flowering vines that MOVED when you weren't looking directly at them. Rooms that had become self-contained ecosystems hosting giant insects, bioluminescent fungi, and fairy creatures who spoke in riddles and got OFFENDED if you solved them too quickly OR too slowly.

The Overgrown Manor was ruled by Lady Aurelian Corvinarus—the fey counterpart to the Shadowfell's vampire lords. Same family, different dimensional branch. Where the Shadowfell operated through undead hierarchy and blood politics, Lady Aurelian ran her court through fey logic. Obligations. Favors. Riddles. Social debts that multiplied if you acknowledged them and TRIPLED if you didn't.

Waluigi spent what felt like DAYS navigating social dynamics that changed based on the time of day, the phase of the moon, and apparently the ambient mood of local butterfly populations. Fey court politics made Mushroom Kingdom diplomacy look STRAIGHTFORWARD.

At least with spiders, you know where you stand. You're standing in a web and the spider wants to eat you. SIMPLE. With fey, you're standing in a conversation and the fairy wants you to owe them something, but they won't tell you WHAT or WHEN, and asking creates ANOTHER obligation.

Toad Lee was surprisingly good company for this ordeal. Quiet. Observant. Didn't trigger accidental fairy obligations by making eye contact with the wrong flower.

**THE DEEP MIRROR — Fractured Atrium**

Markop, Remi, and the Oracle vanished into the Deep Mirror, which was the WORST of the three by a significant margin.

The Deep Mirror was a dimension of crystalline structures, gravity that changed direction without warning, and time that DECAYED. Not just moved differently—DECAYED. Like fruit left on a counter. Things aged visibly. Edges frayed. The dimension was consuming itself and wanted to take everything inside along for the ride.

Waluigi did NOT end up in the Deep Mirror and he is GRATEFUL. The Feywild was exhausting but at least it was ALIVE. The Deep Mirror was DYING, and dying dimensions are apparently not pleasant places to be trapped.

**THE PHYSICAL PLANE — Ritual Room**

The ritual room—the only piece of Raventree Manor that stayed in normal reality—was seized by the Iron Legion within HOURS. Because the Iron Legion has the tactical instincts of a vulture and the moral compass of a calculator.

They recognized the room as an anchor point connecting the three fractured dimensions and immediately secured it. They also sent Toadburt into the Feywild as a coerced operative, fitted with an Entropy Ring to ensure compliance.

Waluigi has strong feelings about strapping obedience collars on people and sending them into alien dimensions. Those feelings can be summarized as: the Iron Legion is AWFUL.

## The Aftermath (Still Ongoing)


The Planar Fracture became the defining catastrophe of everything that followed. Every subsequent battle, alliance, betrayal, and desperate scramble for survival happened in its shadow.

The party was separated across three hostile dimensions with no way to communicate, no way to coordinate, and no way to know if the others were even alive. Waluigi spent every moment in the Feywild wondering whether Archie was dead in the Shadowfell, whether Markop was lost in the Deep Mirror, whether anyone was coming to help or whether 'help' was a concept that had fractured along with reality.

The Iron Legion controlled the only stable anchor point. Because of COURSE they did.

And throughout all of it, Waluigi remembered that he had RAISED CONCERNS. He had ASKED if anyone else was worried. He had been SHUSHED.

Waluigi survived the Feywild. Waluigi survived the fairy courts and the giant insects and the sentient vegetation and Lady Aurelian's INTERMINABLE riddle games. Waluigi survived because Waluigi is TOO STUBBORN to be destroyed by a dimensional catastrophe caused by people who didn't listen to him.

The universe has tried to break Waluigi many times. It has NEVER succeeded.

WAH.

## Lessons Learned (That Nobody Will Remember)


1. **Listen to Waluigi when he raises concerns.** This should be obvious but apparently requires stating explicitly.

2. **Do not build reality-altering rituals on Archie Miser's magic.** His magic is unstable. Everyone knows this. USE SOMEONE ELSE.

3. **Perform important rituals during business hours.** 01:30 AM is not a time for delicate magical work. It's a time for SLEEPING.

4. **Have backup plans for dimensional scatter.** Communication devices that work across planes. Meeting points. SOMETHING.

5. **The Iron Legion will exploit any opportunity.** Plan accordingly.

Waluigi does not expect anyone to remember these lessons. Waluigi has been giving good advice his entire life and watching people ignore it. But Waluigi is putting this on RECORD so that when everything goes wrong AGAIN, Waluigi can point here and say 'WALUIGI TOLD YOU.'

Because Waluigi DID tell them. And they shushed him.

They SHUSHED him.

Waluigi will NEVER forgive the shushing.

description:
Waluigi is going to document this event in full because it represents a new category of catastrophe — not dimensional collapse, not architectural malice, not ritual failure — but the specific horror of watching a party member get turned into ART and then SOLD.

## The Medusa (Who Nobody Thought to Mention Was


There)

Raventree Manor has a Medusa. This information was not in any briefing Waluigi received. Nobody said 'by the way, there is a creature living in this building whose PRIMARY ABILITY is turning people to stone.' Nobody left a NOTE. The warnings Waluigi found previously said 'don't clean the mirrors.' They did NOT say 'don't make eye contact with the resident Gorgon.' Waluigi considers this a significant gap in the available documentation.

The Medusa — a person, technically, a being with a face and clothing and apparently a SCHEDULE — turned Remi to stone with a glare. One glare. That was all it took. Remi made eye contact, the Medusa said something approximately translatable as 'smile,' and Remi became a statue. Remi, who has survived things that would have broken seasoned adventurers, who has walked through chaos with a cheerfulness that Waluigi finds simultaneously admirable and EXHAUSTING, was reduced to decorative stonework in SECONDS.

Then the Medusa put on a paper bag. Over her face. As if this were a reasonable and normal thing to do. And she walked into another room. Waluigi watched this happen. Waluigi has no explanation for the paper bag. Waluigi has filed the paper bag under 'things about this building that will haunt him' alongside the mirror warnings and the servant uniforms with no servants inside them.

## The Library Discovery (Where the Imps Were)


Before the auction could be located, the party needed to navigate the library. The library contained imps — flying, scribing creatures who wrote down everything the party said and did, instantly and in real time. Every statement. Every expression of confusion. Every muttered complaint. Documented.

Waluigi finds the imps philosophically interesting and practically INFURIATING. On one hand, Waluigi APPRECIATES thorough documentation. Waluigi IS thorough documentation. Waluigi understands the value of a complete record. On the other hand, the imps were documenting for the ARCHIVIST — a vampire, presumably, who sat behind a one-way mirror and watched visitors with academic detachment — and their documentation was being used against the party in real time.

Markop also noticed a statue of Vivesna in the library. Vivesna, who Markop killed. Standing there as if to say: 'Hello. Did you think there would be no record?' The manor keeps records of EVERYTHING. Every death. Every deed. Every person turned to stone and auctioned.

## The Archivist (One-Way Mirror,


Infinite Condescension)

The Archivist's room was locked. Eager attempted to pick the lock. The window swung open and the Archivist informed them — with what Waluigi can only describe as vampire SMUG — that one cannot see vampires in mirrors because mirrors don't show them. One-way glass. Eager fell to the floor.

The Archivist then handed the party a poster. An OFFICIAL POSTER. Printed and distributed. It read: 'Official Art Display feat. Archie Miser' — with an image of Remi, turned to stone, presented as an art piece titled after ARCHIE, who WAS NOT EVEN THERE.

Waluigi needs to pause and register his objections. Remi was turned to stone. Remi was classified as an art piece. The art piece was named after Archie, who had nothing to do with this situation, simply because Archie's name apparently means something in this building's social hierarchy. Remi, who was ACTUALLY THERE and is a REAL PERSON, was reduced to supporting cast in her own petrification. Waluigi finds this offensive on multiple levels and intends to remember it.

## The Auction (Twelve Thousand Gold)


The auction room was accessed through a window that Markop used as an observation point before the situation required direct intervention. Through the window, the party watched a bidding war in progress. Remi — Remi, who Waluigi has watched dodge danger with the cheerfulness of someone who doesn't fully process that danger is dangerous — stood at the front of the room as stone. Inert. Sold.

Purple T won. Twelve thousand gold. The winning bidder — who would later identify himself as Mystic Morel — stood up and with an authority that suggested he did this regularly, freed Remi from her stone state. Then announced that she 'belonged to him.'

Waluigi has strong feelings about the phrase 'she belongs to me' and those feelings can be summarized as: NO. Waluigi does not care what was bid. Waluigi does not care what auction rules say. People are not PROPERTY and the Raventree auction house — which is apparently a THING that EXISTS — can take its entire operating structure and throw it into the ocean.

## The Room Erupts (Bowser's Finest Moment)


Markop broke the window. This was the correct response. Waluigi endorses window-breaking as a valid tactical option when the alternative is watching a party member get claimed as a purchased item.

The chaos that followed was, in Waluigi's assessment, textbook Disaster Inc. Wario appeared — from WHERE, Waluigi does not know, Wario simply APPEARS in chaotic situations like a bad omen in mustache form — and shoulder-barged Markop to the floor. A mages guild operative materialized and claimed Remi for THEMSELVES. Bowser pulled out a device to call his son for backup, which is either terrifying or comforting depending on how you feel about Koopa reinforcements. Markop summoned a moonbeam. Mystic Morel jumped out a window.

Salam started picking flowers. Waluigi does not have context for this. Waluigi has CHOSEN not to pursue context for this.

Remi ran out and jumped into Dan's arms. The auction was over.

## The Aftermath (Mystic Morel, Persistent Problem)


Remi was free. Remi was also standing next to Mystic Morel, who had jumped out the window and apparently landed directly into the aftermath of the situation he caused, which Waluigi considers AUDACIOUS.

Mystic Morel — Purple T, winning bidder, self-described owner of a person — explained himself with what the toads assessed as a LIE. He then offered tea. He offered incense. He insisted on following Remi 'to keep his end of the deal,' a deal that Remi had no memory of making, which is the most concerning detail of an extremely concerning afternoon.

A deal. With someone Remi doesn't remember. For a price she can't recall. Mystic Morel insists it exists. Remi cannot confirm or deny it. Waluigi has placed Mystic Morel in the category of 'problems that are currently walking around behind the party and have not been resolved.' That category is unfortunately crowded.

Wario also reappeared with a debt list the length of the mansion. Bowser owes him money. The list was long enough to cross a single item off and still remain longer than most legal documents Waluigi has encountered. Wario claimed the bomb he once gave Remi in a box was 'incidental.' Waluigi does not believe anything involving Wario is incidental. Wario is the OPPOSITE of incidental. Wario is purpose made.

title: The Ruined Manor Dossier — Blood Trails, a Silent Blast, and the Portal Problem
date: 1040 BF — exact date and sequence under review
