summary: This dossier continues directly from Kaelor Judi’s witness-line expedition to Raventree. Once the improvised coalition reaches the Ruined Manor, Toad Lee’s “Ryan” disguise, Sprig’s bloodied Legion photograph, Slick’s contradictory massacre cover story, Agent L’s portal-closing proposal, and Byscilla Danos’s guarded authority expose a manor already failing across planes.
description:
Waluigi is filing this one as its own dossier because it introduces an entirely new cast — Toad Lee posing as 'Ryan,' Agent L operating a Poltergust under the alias Luigi, a Legion officer named Byscilla Danos, a mole calling himself Sprig, and a fugitive named Archie who has not yet appeared but who every other character in this session seems to want something from. Waluigi has no prior file to connect this to. He intends to build one from scratch, starting now, and he is already unhappy with what he is finding. WAH.

## The Closet — A Massacre, a Lie About It, and a Second, Contradicting Lie


The session opens with Toad Lee — going by Ryan, for reasons Waluigi has not yet been given and intends to ask about later — alone in a closet, having separated from his group and locked himself in. Voices outside: *'was the toad in here, check that door.'* A door opens. *'It's clear, no one is here.'* A curse. *'Stay on your post, we will check outside.'*

Ryan waited it out, peeked out once it was quiet, heard scuttling, then a skull crack, then laughter, then the door opened on its own. It was Sprig — a mole, knife in hand, freshly bloodied.

*'Who else would it be, the Legion?'* he laughed.

Asked who he'd just killed, Sprig admitted he genuinely wasn't certain — *'they all blend in, mages guild, legion, what's the difference, there's just a new suit in a coat of armor.'* He then produced, unprompted, a photograph: himself smiling, flanked by two unidentified figures in Legion uniform, also smiling, the whole image speckled with blood. Ryan told him to put it back. He did.

*Waluigi wants to open with this photograph specifically, because it is the strangest object in the entire session and nobody who saw it asked a single follow-up question. Sprig is carrying a photograph of himself smiling alongside Legion soldiers who are also smiling, and the photo itself is covered in blood — not blood from the moment Sprig showed it, but blood already on the print, meaning the photograph was either taken during or immediately after some prior violent event, and Sprig has been carrying it around ever since as a keepsake. A man does not keep a bloodied photo of himself grinning next to soldiers he now claims not to be able to distinguish from anyone else he's killing.

Either that photo documents the last time Sprig knew, with certainty, who his allies were — before whatever happened to blur that line for him — or it documents something Sprig did to those two Legion figures personally, and he is carrying the evidence as a trophy rather than a memory.

Waluigi does not have enough information yet to choose between these readings.

He is filing the photograph as unfinished business.

WAH.*

Sprig also admitted, when pressed for a compass or a map, that he had neither and didn't need one: *'who needs a compass when you have the blood to follow.'* Ryan told him plainly he wasn't inspiring much confidence. Sprig agreed, cheerfully, that he was leading them into trouble. Ryan told him he couldn't trust him. Sprig didn't argue.

Ryan pushed on alone through the grove, out into the main courtyard — and stopped cold at what he found there. The transcript does not say what it was. Ryan's only words to Sprig, once he'd composed himself enough to speak: *'you did all this?'* Sprig, notably, was already gone by that point. Ryan was alone when he asked the question out loud to no one.

*Waluigi wants to be very precise about the sequence here, because it matters more than the missing description does. Ryan asked 'you did all this' directed at Sprig — but Sprig was not present to hear it. Ryan asked an absent man a question about a horror he refused to describe even to himself, in his own account of the session. Waluigi has seen this shape before, in a different file entirely: a person choosing not to look directly at something in order to keep functioning. Waluigi will not speculate about the content of what Ryan saw, because Waluigi was not shown it and does not believe in inventing atrocities that weren't described to him.

But Waluigi does want to note that whatever it was, it was bad enough that Ryan retreated to a cottage afterward and simply let time pass rather than process it on the spot.

That is worth remembering for what comes two scenes later.

WAH.*

## The Cottage — Koopa's Explanation, and the Explanation That Undoes It

Some time later, a knock. Koopa, checking in — *'you doing alright? sorry about the scare, Sprig played a trick.'* Ryan, still shaken but composed, went along with it. They headed back out. Fewer bodies than before.

*'I guess some of them are decomposing,'* Ryan offered. *'The sixth stage has come.'*

Koopa panicked at this — *'no no no, we knocked them out, and we smeared blood all over to make it look like a massacre, to scare the Legion away'* — and the transcript itself flags, in the same breath, the obvious problem: *(was this a lie?)*

*Waluigi wants to lay the two explanations side by side, because they cannot both be true and nobody in the scene forced the issue. Explanation one, offered by Koopa on the spot: the bodies are not corpses, they were unconscious people, blood was smeared on for staging purposes, a deception aimed at scaring off the Legion. Explanation two, which Ryan himself volunteered a moment earlier without prompting: there are fewer bodies now than before, and the ones remaining show visible decomposition consistent with the passage of real time. Decomposition is not something you can stage. A body that is rotting is a body that was dead when it started rotting, or has been dead long enough since to visibly change.

If Koopa's story were true — unconscious people, staged blood, no actual deaths — there would be no bodies decomposing at all, because there would be no actual dead bodies to decompose in the first place.

There is no version of 'we faked a massacre with unconscious people and paint' that produces a scene with fewer, more decayed corpses a few hours later.

Someone is lying to Ryan here, and Waluigi is fairly confident it is Koopa, because Koopa is the one who supplied an explanation immediately, unprompted, before Ryan had asked for one — which is precisely the behavior of someone covering rather than someone recounting.

Waluigi is also noting, quietly, that this is now the second time in this entire investigative record — Waluigi is thinking specifically of a certain skeleton and a certain war — that a companion has offered a comforting explanation for something horrific that does not survive basic scrutiny, and has done so instantly and unprompted rather than reluctantly.

Waluigi does not yet know if these two patterns are related.

He is old enough now to stop assuming coincidence.

WAH.*

## Sneaking Through the Grounds — Archie, Rocks as Distractions, and a Torch Declined

Moving through the grounds, guards patrolling, Ryan threw a rock to draw a patrol away, declined Koopa's offer of a torch — *'not yet, if they see they will jump us,' 'torch is our vision and weapon,'* handing it off rather than carrying it lit — and laid out his operating principle plainly: *'we sneak around, only fight when we can, because I'm a rogue, you understand, Koopa?'* Koopa — revealed here, offhandedly, to actually go by 'Slick' — agreed to hold back for the day despite preferring a fight, and mentioned, in passing, a toad friend who shares his taste for combat.

Hiding again from voices, Ryan overheard mention of 'Thornbury' being mistaken for 'the purple toad,' and used the moment to reveal his actual agenda for the first time out loud: he intends to get the drop on Archie for revenge — Archie stole his journal and still owes him money — and plans to file an official Legion report on him, 'rat him out,' and set off a chain of events by going up into the mountains. The transcript notes, tersely, that this has 'happened before,' tied to a prior teleport to something called the Alpine Bank.

*Waluigi wants to flag Archie's growing shape carefully, because he is the only character in this entire session who has not yet appeared and who is nonetheless the stated motive of at least three different people. Sprig wants to find him, or at least follows blood in his general direction. Ryan wants him for a stolen journal and unpaid debt, and has apparently pursued this same grievance through at least one prior loop of events, given the 'this has happened before' aside about the Alpine Bank teleport. And, as Waluigi will get to shortly, the Mages Guild wants to recruit him for reasons a mage describes only as 'manic.' A man who is simultaneously a debtor, a target of Legion-adjacent violence, and a recruitment prospect for a magical institution, before he has said a single word on the page, is not an incidental character.

Archie is the gravity well this entire session orbits.

Waluigi has not met him yet and is already building a file.

WAH.*

## Ambush by Agent L — the Poltergust, and the Kitchen Device That Could Undo Every Portal in the World

Entering a room, Ryan was tackled and had a vacuum device pressed to his face before Agent L — Luigi — recognized him and let go. Once weapons were lowered, the conversation turned immediately, and with startling casualness, to something enormous: a device in the kitchen that could close the portals connecting this location to other planes entirely.

Luigi laid out the stakes with a precision that undercuts his own goofy delivery: closing the portal here risks 'creating' two additional planes — 'blueward' and 'orangeward' — of unknown character. Ryan pushed back — what happens to the people currently on the other side, mid-transit, if the portal closes while they're using it? Luigi's answer, delivered with the same shrugging confidence throughout: the collapse is localized, other portals presumably exist elsewhere, and anyone caught in the closure would likely be 'popped out' at the nearest inflection point, landing in the arms of either the Mages Guild or the Legion.

Pressed on what happens if there is no other portal to pop out to, Luigi's answer was, verbatim, that they'd 'be stuck forever, but I'm sure that will never happen.'

*Waluigi needs the reader to actually stop and register what was just agreed to here, because it was agreed to in the tone of two people discussing whether to take the stairs or the elevator. Luigi is describing a device capable of permanently trapping an unknown number of people in a plane of existence with no way home, and his risk assessment for this outcome is 'I'm sure that will never happen' — not because he has evidence it won't happen, but because he would simply prefer not to think about it happening. This is the single largest unexamined decision in the entire session, larger by orders of magnitude than anything involving Sprig's photograph or Koopa's contradicted lie, and it was waved through in about four lines of dialogue by two people who, by their own admission, don't fully understand what the device does.

Waluigi wants this flagged clearly: somewhere in this story's future, someone is going to ask what happened to whoever was using a portal at the moment it got closed, and 'Luigi said it'd probably be fine' is not going to be a satisfying answer.

WAH.*

## The Silent Field — A Spell That Backfires on Its Own Caster

Moving deeper, the pair encountered a guard. Koopa/Slick kicked, got dragged off, was rescued by Ryan; Luigi super-jumped and blasted the guard from above with ice. Ryan, meanwhile, cast a large silence field over the confrontation — a genuinely clever tactical instinct, muffling the fight from anyone listening elsewhere in the building.

And then immediately discovered the field's fatal design flaw: every spell Ryan himself had left required a verbal component. He had just neutered his own magic for the duration of a fight he'd chosen to hide.

*Waluigi wants to give this the same credit and the same criticism he gave the Agent's tether improvisation in an entirely different case file, because the shape of the mistake rhymes closely enough to be worth naming directly. A silence field is a genuinely good idea against a threat whose main danger is calling for backup. It is a catastrophically bad idea for a caster whose entire offensive kit runs on spoken incantations, and Ryan appears to have realized this only after the field was already up and the fight was already underway — meaning he designed and deployed a tactical solution to one problem (being overheard) without first checking whether it created a worse problem (being unable to fight back).

This is the exact same failure mode Waluigi has documented before in an entirely different context: a plan executed with real cleverness in its conception and no verification at all of its own side effects.

Ryan is, by his own account, a rogue who prefers not to fight when avoidable.

His own silence field forced him into close, silent, physically brutal combat — a knife into a shell, an acid throw with no verbal trigger required, one final blast so overloaded it damaged his own hand — specifically because the tool he built to avoid a fight removed his ability to avoid this one.

WAH.*

The fight escalated past the edges of the silence field into open combat — Luigi vaulting tables, deflecting a blast into the ceiling, getting pinned to a wall — before Ryan's acid, thrown blind into the dark since he'd also misplaced his torch by this point, connected with the guard and drove him stumbling back into the silent zone, where a final blast finished him in total, visible, unheard silence. The guard did not die outright. He crawled — 'let... me... finish... you' — chasing Ryan uselessly across the floor while Luigi and the guard were left behind as Ryan fled through a window with Agent L's help.

*Waluigi will not dwell on the violence itself, which speaks for itself, but he does want to note the detail of the silent explosion specifically — 'a silent explosion is not heard but seen, a hole is left in the abandoned archive.' A weapon powerful enough to leave a visible crater in a building's structure, discharged with no sound at all because of a field its own user forgot would also gag him, is an image Waluigi finds genuinely unsettling in a way none of the session's jokes quite offset. Ryan won this fight. He also nearly disarmed himself doing it, and the only reason he didn't is that his opponent went down before Ryan needed to cast anything else that required his voice.

WAH.*

## The Library — A Second Guard, Fire Off Glass, and Byscilla Danos

Ryan and Luigi pressed on into an adjoining library — described, in the moment, as an immense collapsed cavern of sagging, gutted bookshelves, its once-priceless collection now 'trodden underfoot... scattered like entrails of dead animals.' Opening a door bumped a guard on the other side, triggering a running chase through the manor before looping back into this same room. Ryan hid behind a shelf; a thrown knife split a book beside his head; he answered with acid. A wild firebolt, aimed at a window, bounced off the glass instead of through it and set the pursuing guard on fire outright.

*Waluigi wants to note the room description on its own merits for a moment, separate from the fight that happened in it, because Waluigi suspects the description is doing more narrative work than anyone intended. A library whose contents have been reduced to illegible, trampled scraps, in a manor already crawling with guards, a mole with a bloodied trophy photo, and a device capable of permanently sealing people into other planes, is not a subtle image. Somebody's records — Waluigi does not yet know whose — have already been destroyed here, long before Ryan and Luigi arrived to add their own violence on top of the wreckage.

Waluigi has, by this point in his overall casework, developed something of an allergy to destroyed archives.

He is noting this library and moving on, for now.

WAH.*

With the guard dead, Luigi shaking, Byscilla Danos arrived — sharp, procedural, clearly an authority figure — and caught Luigi somewhere he apparently wasn't meant to be. Her line to him, half-threat and half-affection: *'we may be allies but that doesn't mean I can't follow protocol, come back to find your mustache'* — before informing him she and 'Thornbury' had matters to discuss and taking him by the hand out of the room. Ryan, left behind, managed only a whispered *'I'll figure things out'* before Luigi was gone.

*Waluigi wants this moment flagged for what it reveals about Byscilla specifically: she is procedural, she outranks Luigi in some functional sense, she refers to 'Thornbury' as someone she has business with independent of this entire chase, and she extracted Luigi from an active combat scene with total physical ease, hand in hand, without resistance from him. Waluigi will have more to say about Byscilla by the end of this file, because her later behavior recontextualizes this entrance considerably. For now: she is the second character in this session, after Sprig, to physically remove a companion from Ryan's side without much explanation.

Ryan is very good at losing his allies one at a time.

WAH.*

## Alone in the Manor — a Captured Ally, a Starving Merchant, and Eight Hours Lost to Sleep

Ryan, now alone, heard someone else get surrounded in the main hall through a peephole — a hammer brother, dragged off by guards — and made the deliberate choice not to intervene, magically locking his own door instead and turning his attention back to testing whether his acid still worked on a corpse. He rested behind a bookshelf. His sleep was interrupted by boots: a merchant, Hargam Fidger, offering wares. Ryan, out of rations, could afford only arrows and a mace, had nothing to sell, and the merchant left hungry — prompting Ryan to privately resolve to simply steal from him if their paths crossed again.

Ryan then took a full eight-hour rest.

When he returned to a previously visited room, he found a mage and a hammer brother alive, having taken shelter through a trapdoor — the same hammer brother captured earlier, evidently having survived or escaped — and their reaction to Ryan's eight hours of sleep was blunt disbelief: *'do you know how long we've been trying to survive out here without food, water, or anything, and you just slept.'* They then delivered the operational news of the session: the Legion's supply convoy 'got caught up in something,' nobody knows what, and rations for this entire division are running critically low.

*Waluigi wants to connect two things that are sitting several scenes apart in this transcript and were not connected by anyone inside it. The Legion's supply convoy is missing, its cause unknown, and this division is starving as a direct result. Meanwhile, earlier in this same session, Ryan personally chose not to intervene when a hammer brother was surrounded and dragged off by guards, in order to keep his own position secure — a hammer brother who then reappears, alive, having apparently escaped on his own, angry specifically about how much time and how many resources have been lost while everyone else scrambled to survive.

Ryan's私 caution bought him safety at the exact moment his allies were running out of food.

Waluigi is not moralizing about this — hiding was, tactically, probably correct — but he wants it on the record that the cost of Ryan's caution was paid by someone else, and that person is now standing in the room aware of it.

WAH.*

## The Planar Bleed — Shadowfell Air, a Feywild Root, and a Warning From Byscilla

And then, without warning, the environment itself spoke. The floor beneath a fresh crater 'softened like wet paper' and dropped another foot with a wet, grinding sound. Cold, colourless air rose from the gap — Shadowfell air, the kind that makes fire sputter and blood run thick. A single grey root, bleeding in from the Feywild, tasted the blood on the stones and withdrew. Luigi, elsewhere in the corridor with Byscilla, felt the same pressure change in his ears; the Poltergust gave an involuntary whir. Byscilla's own verdict, flat and immediate: *'that was not structural. Move.'*

*Waluigi needs to slow down for this passage specifically, because it is the first moment in this entire session where the setting itself, rather than any character, delivers direct information, and Waluigi trusts unprompted environmental behavior far more than he trusts anything any of these people have told each other so far. A root that tastes blood on stone and withdraws is not random set dressing — it is a described behavior, an action with intent, performed by something bleeding through from an entirely separate plane in direct response to violence that already happened in this room. Combine this with the earlier device conversation — a machine sitting in this same manor's kitchen that is explicitly capable of creating new planes, 'blueward' or 'orangeward,' as an unintended side effect of trying to close existing portals — and Waluigi is no longer willing to treat the Shadowfell/Feywild bleed as background flavor.

Something in this manor is already leaking between planes before anyone has touched the kitchen device.

Whatever Luigi's machine is meant to fix, it may not be creating the problem from scratch.

It may be trying to close a door that was already coming open on its own.

Byscilla clearly knows this instinctively — 'that was not structural' is not a guess, it's a diagnosis, delivered instantly, by someone who did not need to see the root to know what she was dealing with.

Waluigi is beginning to suspect Byscilla Danos knows a great deal more about this manor's actual condition than her 'Legion protocol' introduction let on.

WAH.*

## The Mages Guild's Room — Ambient Magic, a Rare Toad Mage, and a Trap Ryan Builds and

Then Abandons

Reunited with Luigi and Byscilla — who nearly ran Ryan through on sight before Luigi vouched for him — the group was led to the one room in the manor occupied by the Mages Guild. A mage there explained, cheerfully, that the machines powering the manor's 'tapestry' also power the portals, and that the Guild has connected its own network to analyze ambient magic in the area — 'just not in the kitchen, the machines are in there, and rust monsters, dead ones.' The mage mentioned, in passing, having once mentored a rare toad recruit who became 'a fine mage.'

Ryan, noting he couldn't personally feel any of this supposedly detectable ambient magic himself, filed it under 'higher level mage skill' and let it go — while simultaneously signaling, behind his own back, for two hidden allies to hold position for an ambush he was quietly planning against Byscilla. He convinced Agent L to help slam her into a wall, reasoning this would let Luigi finally break free of her oversight and go retrieve the kitchen device himself. Luigi, notably, refused outright when asked directly, and only the sound of a struggle from a nearby room minutes later revealed that a different plan had been executed instead: Koopa/Slick and a mage were found unconscious, and it was Luigi himself, tripping over his own feet, who stumbled into the wizard's room in the aftermath.

*Waluigi wants this section flagged as the moment Ryan's own instincts finally, briefly, get the better of him — and then, notably, don't. He built the setup for an ambush on an ally, signaled his own hidden allies to prepare for a fight, and then simply did not go through with the version of the plan he'd actually proposed. Someone else knocked out Koopa and the mage instead, off-screen, and Ryan's own confrontation with Byscilla, when it finally came, was not violence at all — it was a conversation. Waluigi finds this genuinely notable given everything Ryan has done up to this point in the session: he has stabbed a guard, thrown acid blind in the dark, planned an ambush on a Legion officer he'd only just met properly — and then, given the actual opportunity to hurt her, he talked instead.

Waluigi does not think this is an accident of the scene.

He thinks it is the first real character choice Ryan has made all session that wasn't purely tactical.

WAH.*

## Toad Lee, a Note Left for No One, and a Conversation That Finally Says the Quiet Part

While Ryan and Byscilla talked, a fifth thread resolved itself quietly: Toad Lee — wandering the manor 'flying solo' — found the earlier unconscious guard, hammer brother, and mage, with Luigi standing over them, failed to wake them, dragged them instead to the library as a makeshift base, and left behind a note: *'We're with the red-haired lady but not as present, in disguise, you need to be discrete, I'm pretending to be on her side, do whatever you think is right.'*

*Waluigi wants this note flagged specifically because of who it was left for: unconscious people. Toad Lee wrote an operational security briefing and left it beside three people who were not conscious to read it, with no guarantee any of them would wake before Byscilla or anyone else found it first. This is either an act of genuine, if slightly panicked, good faith — trying to warn allies the moment they wake, before he can be there to explain in person — or it is a liability Toad Lee created without thinking through who else might read a note that plainly states an ongoing deception of a Legion officer, left in a room that Legion officer has already once walked into personally.

Waluigi is filing this note next to the photograph Sprig showed off earlier in the session: two documents, in one afternoon, that a more careful operative would not have left lying around.

WAH.*

Then, finally, Ryan pulled Agent L aside for the conversation the entire session had been circling without landing. Was Byscilla friend or foe? *'She's uh... my boss,'* Luigi admitted. Ryan absorbed this. Luigi went further: she 'isn't too nice, but she has a good heart' — he mostly does this for money, though he 'wishes he could go back to good old days.' Ryan agreed he understood that feeling. And then the actual question, asked plainly, without deflection: *long term, what's important to you, money or friends?*

Luigi's answer, after a hesitation the transcript itself renders as a long trailing pause: *'friends... but you need to realize you're not my only friend here, I won't betray you, in fact I'll work with you, but maybe we can work something out where you don't have to join the guild or harm any of my mage friends.'* Ryan didn't fully commit either way, but Luigi laid out the actual line for him regardless: the Mages Guild isn't the Legion — 'less cruel' — and, strangest of all, they apparently want to recruit Archie 'for some manic reason,' the same Archie Ryan has been chasing all session for a debt and a stolen journal.

Ryan's final position, given without much elaboration: he'll knock Byscilla out if it comes to that, but not kill her.

Luigi's closing line, quiet and pointed: *'she must be someone dear to you.

I will keep that in mind.'*

*Waluigi wants to end on this exchange because it is the only moment in the entire session where anyone stated their actual loyalties out loud, without a joke immediately undercutting it. Luigi works for Byscilla for money and misses 'the old days.' He values friends over money when finally forced to choose, but refuses to promise he'll actively fight beside Ryan against his own guild if it comes to that — only that he won't stop Ryan, and won't use full force against his own people either. That is not an alliance. That is a very carefully worded non-aggression pact between two people who like each other and do not, in fact, share a side.

And Luigi's closing line to Ryan — 'she must be someone dear to you' — was said about Byscilla, a woman Ryan has known for roughly one scene, based on nothing but the fact that Ryan chose to talk rather than fight her.

Waluigi suspects Luigi knows something about Byscilla that he still has not told Ryan directly, and that this entire conversation, warm as it reads, was Luigi quietly finding out how far Ryan could be pushed before deciding it was time to find out.

WAH.*

Waluigi is correcting the location without deleting the account that was already written: this is the **Ruined Manor at Raventree**, not a separate Thornwood site. The preceding Kaelor Judi witness-line record ends with Luigi’s witness list, Kaelor, Ryan, Slick, Sprig, and the other loose witnesses turning toward this exact house. The office was a staging area disguised as a claims office. The road to Raventree was where the witness line became the group now entering the ruin. An archive should preserve where it was wrong as well as where it became less wrong.

That continuity changes the opening closet scene. Ryan is not merely a rogue who happens to meet Sprig in an unfamiliar house. He arrives from the coalition Kaelor watched form around Markop, Archie, the Vigilance, Barrel Toad logistics, and the Pond Patrol intercepts. Sprig’s claim that unpaid debt is why he helps Markop now sits beside the bloodied photograph and the blood-trail method he offers Ryan. Luigi’s interest in Archie is not an isolated errand either; it is the concealed additional reason he was already moving the witness list toward Raventree. The group entered under aliases and partial stories before the first guard was even encountered.

The Pond Patrol material remains relevant even when no patrol member enters the room. Kaelor recovered communications treating Raventree as a target or objective, describing toad movements and rally points, connecting the pyromancer hunt to Archie’s trail, and carrying the full We Are the Toads transcript among intelligence that was clearly not as frivolous as it looked. The missing convoy, guard presence, and pressure around portal machinery are happening at a site other organized groups independently marked as important. Waluigi’s favorite kind of coincidence is the kind that stops being one after the third faction arrives.

This also sharpens the danger in Slick’s explanation. If the massacre was staged, he is concealing an operation from allies who need to know what ground they are crossing. If it was not, he is using the language of staging to launder something far worse into tactical necessity. “We smeared blood to scare the Legion” makes fear the method and asks Ryan to accept bodies as props without inspecting the evidence. Either reading is an unacceptable intelligence practice.

The ruined manor is damaged infrastructure, not merely a battlefield. Ryan’s silent blast may reveal the planar breach rather than create it; the library is already gutted, the guards are coordinated, and the building answers violence with Shadowfell cold and a Feywild root that reacts to blood. Byscilla is the person most likely to recognize that distinction. Her immediate “that was not structural” is neither proof she is harmless nor proof she is lying. It is evidence that she can prioritize survival over protocol when reality begins leaking through the floor.

No group present has adequate custody of the portal device. Luigi knows possible outcomes but cannot guarantee them. The Guild understands part of the tapestry but does not visibly control the kitchen. The Legion has guards and a failing convoy but no demonstrated technical authority. Ryan and Toad Lee have initiative but work through disguise, improvisation, and unsecured notes. The Pond Patrol has external interest but no visible representation. Everyone holds one piece of authority and nobody holds enough to shut a door between worlds safely. That is exactly how someone makes a unilateral decision, calls it necessary, and leaves everyone else to discover its cost.

Waluigi’s expanded ruling is that Raventree is where every institution arrives with a partial map and mistakes it for jurisdiction. The Legion sees security, the Guild sees an arcane system, the Pond Patrol sees a target or rally point, Ryan sees Archie, Kaelor sees Markop, Sprig sees debt, and Luigi sees friends on more than one side. The manor sees none of these categories and continues to bleed. Until the witnesses compare evidence before another portal, another silence field, or another convenient lie, the Ruined Manor will keep turning separate missions into the same disaster. WAH.
